struggle.what_happened: The radiologist reported a small pneumothorax (air outside the lung) at the right apex. FindXRay correctly found the opacity in the right lower lung, but wrote "no pneumothorax", and its own checking steps approved that sentence.
why: The finding is a thin line at the very top of the lung: a few pixels once the whole X-ray is reduced to the size the AI reads.
Similar-case search compares whole images, which captures large patterns (heart size, lung volume) well but small local findings poorly (measured in the encoder benchmark).
The checker is the same model family as the writer, so it tends to agree with the draft: it approved 98.6% of sentences across the evaluation.
fix: Zoom-in second look: crop the lung tops and corners at full resolution and ask targeted questions (pneumothorax, small effusions) before the report is finalised.
Add a dedicated pneumothorax detector as a tool the agent must consult, instead of relying on the language model's eyes alone.
Use a different, stronger model as the checker, so it does not share the writer's blind spots.
